propositions: Rebar must support credentials for Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira Cloud/DC across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, AWS-hosted, CLI, library, MCP, and hosted-service consumers without weakening SDK-native refresh or credential-helper protection.

Upstream SDKs, helpers, and CI systems own credential issuance, retrieval, persistence, refresh, rotation, and invalidation; Rebar owns only safe passage through typed bindings, operation-scoped construction, and fail-closed provider selection.

Static secret rotation for long-running processes is restart/redeploy based; short-lived CLI processes receive current startup environment; Rebar will not poll, retrieve, watch, or maintain hot-reload secret cache.

Deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM or equivalent) before process startup; Rebar accepts provider-native credentials and narrowly scoped static secrets only at adapter boundaries via REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (preferred) or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY.

Trusted same-capability child processes inherit ambient environment for compatibility; Rebar materializes static credentials only onto owning children, removes exact sibling-secret variable names, and never mutates global os.environ.
Unavoidable static credentials use Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes only in provider-specific non-serializable containers excluded from repr, comparison, hashing, caching, and operation snapshots.
